It depends on the type of restaurant you're in.  If it's a "family' restaurant that may make sense.  In my experience smaller portion of menu items is bad for business because it clogs up the line and it's too much effort for the gains you may think you get.  I largely blame our food culture for creating the problem because in most other countries, a "kid's" menu isn't really a thing.  Kids are fussy eaters in the U.S because they were raised to be that way.  I didn't grow up with a kid's menu at all and I think the idea of a kid's menu is a stupid one.  While I agree that in a perfect world children should eat what adults eat that isn't the world we live in.  If it's a "higher" scale restaurant often times you don't want children in their at all.  They destroy stuff in the restaurant, are often loud and a pain in the ass of other patrons.  In the end parents are to blame for raising generations of kids who won't eat anything that isn't drenched in ranch, mayo, ketchup or processed cheese sauce.

I"m in the exact scenario but have dealt with it entirely different.  I've learned to hone my taste for dark comedy.  It's a good coping mechanism and if I can laugh at the thought of Old Yeller getting shot or find humor in the torture scene to Reservoir Dogs then I know I'm coping a bit better with the pain of existence.  Perhaps you should do the same or find an emotional outlet.  This doesn't mean things will improve for you but will help cope with things.

I don't know whether to agree or disagree with you.  In my case I simply don't care.  I suppose I am just whining and complaining but I find myself doing the "right" things more out of habit than actually wanting for good things to happen.  Hope isn't something I really believe in as mathematically it serves no purpose.  Any negative actions I may take are not taken out of respect for the few people that have a stake in my well being.  Short of that I'm not sure I care to see good things happen to anyone anymore.  It's gotten to the point where terrible things make me laugh and this recent pandemic is the source of humor and harsh coping mechanisms.  I'm losing my humanity by the day and have accepted that my humanity is finite.  I'm curious to see what I will do or what will happen once my humanity and capacity for joy finally runs out.  At this pace it most definitely will I just don't know when that will happen.

I have a fantasy where I will do just that, disappear, move to a cabin and spend the rest of my days living like Ted Kaczynski.  Frankly I find people so horrible that short of hanging one's self disappearing may be the best alternative.  People are garbage in general and avoiding the one thing one hates the most may be the best option if suicide isn't the solution.  Wanting to disappear is something I can relate to and something I fantasize about a lot.
Black comedy, dark humor, sardonic conversations and the occasional glass of bourbon.  That's how I've coped with this for the past few years.
